text_blocks.snippet: While there is currently no cure for multiple sclerosis (MS), significant advancements in treatment have been made, particularly in disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). These therapies aim to reduce the frequency and severity of MS attacks and slow disease progression. Recent developments include new oral medications, monoclonal antibodies, and even potential breakthroughs in stem cell therapy.

list.snippet: The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation to tolebrutinib, an investigational oral medication, for non-relapsing secondary-progressive MS (nrSPMS). This designation signifies the potential for substantial improvement over existing therapies for this form of MS, where individuals experience progressive disability without relapses.
